injury to the sciatic nerve induces changes in sodium channel mRNA and protein expression in neurons in the ventroposterolateral (VLP) nucleus of the rat thalamus, and that this change is associated with increased spontaneous firing and enhanced responsiveness to peripheral stimuli.

peripheral nerve injury induces changes in sodium channel and glutamate receptor expression within third-order VPL nociceptive neurons and that this change is associated with increased background firing, increased responsiveness to peripheral stimulation, and increased responsiveness to glutamate.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

injury to the periphery induces changes in the expression of sodium channels within the dorsal horn, thalamus, and cortex, which contribute to the hyperexcitability and hyperresponsiveness of these neurons and contribute to the development of neuropathic pain.
the expression of sodium channels in pain processing areas in the brain is altered after peripheral nerve injury and that these changes contribute to neuropathic allodynia.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the sodium channels in the thalamus change after nerve injury and that these changes may contribute to the hyperexcitability and hypersensitivity of thalamic cells that is thought to contribute to neuropathic allodynia and pain.
peripheral nerve injury up-regulates sodium channel expression in third-order thalamic pain processing neurons, and this may contribute to the development and maintenance of neuropathic pain.
